content_metadata.description: Exploring the benefits of the EaSatto microfocuser with Celestron EdgeHD telescopes, highlighting its superior focusing capabilities and applications in astrophotography.

qAndA.answer: The internal focusing mechanism, which moves the primary mirror, can cause image shift and mirror flop, affecting the quality of astrophotography images.
qAndA.question: What is the main problem with the internal focusing mechanism of Celestron EdgeHD telescopes?

qAndA.answer: The 2-inch EaSatto's free aperture is already larger than the EdgeHD's internal baffle tube, providing enough clearance. Using a larger EaSatto would not offer any additional benefits.
qAndA.question: Why is the EaSatto 2-inch microfocuser sufficient for EdgeHD telescopes, and why is the 3-inch version not needed?

qAndA.answer: Yes, the EaSatto can be installed after the focal reducer. The focal reducer doesn't change the backfocus requirements, so the EaSatto can still be used for precise focusing.
qAndA.question: Can the EaSatto be used with the EdgeHD focal reducer?

qAndA.answer: By adjusting the draw tube extension, the user can achieve the precise distance required for their camera sensor to be in focus. The EaSatto can then be used for making fine-tuning micro-adjustments without affecting the overall backfocus.
qAndA.question: How does the EaSatto help in achieving perfect backfocus?

qAndA.answer: The EaSatto allows for making micro-focus adjustments without moving the primary mirror, thus eliminating the risk of image shift and mirror flop. This ensures a more stable and precise focus for astrophotography.
qAndA.question: What is the main advantage of using the EaSatto for micro-focus adjustments compared to the internal focuser?

text_to_speech: Hello astronomers! Today I want to show you why the ESATTO is the perfect microfocuser for Celestron EdgeHD and similar telescopes in order to have the best performance in astrophotography! Celestron EdgeHD telescopes, like all the classic Schmidt-Cassegrain telescopes, come with internal focusing mechanism that moves the primary mirror to allow you reach focus with all the eyepieces, with or without mirror diagonal, and with all the astrophotography cameras. But, by moving the primary mirror, you may find problems of image shift and mirror flop that are normal with such an internal focuser. That’s why Celestron added, in the EdgeHD telescopes, a primary mirror locking mechanism that locks the primary mirror in position. But, by doing that, you can’t precisely focus anymore and this is the first great advantage of using an external microfocuser like the ESATTO! So by connecting it to the telescope you can focus with the primary mirror locked, and you have no more image shift and mirror flop! And this brings to the second great advantage of using the ESATTO as external microfocuser. You have primary mirror locked and, at the same time, you can control the focus, also remotely! For example, if you set your astrophotography software to refocus in between long exposition pictures, you can easily refocus all night long, also when you change filters! OK, so I know now you will have many questions, so let’s start! The ESATTO is a microfocuser so it has a short travel. Will it be enough to focus with different eyepieces or different cameras? ok sure! In fact when you change eyepiece, you will need to make just a small focus adjustment. And, if in any case you have to change focus a lot (for example when you remove an eyepiece and install a camera) you can always move the internal focuser first and then use the ESATTO Thank you! The EdgeHD telescopes require the sensor to be at a precise distance from the telescope, is the ESATTO too thick for this? No it’s not. In fact all the EdgeHD telescopes have a long backfocus (133mm for the 8” model, 146mm for all the others) and since the ESATTO 2” is only 67mm thick, you still have a lot of space to properly set your camera sensor. ok, can I use the larger ESATTO 3” microfocuser on my EdgeHD telescope? Well, theoretically you could but it’s not needed. That’s because the ESATTO 2” free aperture is already larger than the EdgeHD internal baffle tube. So a larger ESATTO is really not needed for the EdgeHD telescopes. Wonderful, but I have the EdgeHD focal reducer, can I use it? Of course you can use it, also with the ESATTO microfocuser! The focal reducer is designed to be directly threaded to the rear cell of the telescope because the lens group has to be at a precise distance from the internal flattener. One of the greatest features of these telescopes is that the focal reducer doesn’t change the back focus requirements in 9.25”, 11” and 14” models. So, if you properly set the backfocus without the reducer, you can install the ESATTO microfocuser after the reducer and it will work in the same way. Only in the 8” model, the backfocus is reduced from 133mm (without reducer) to 105mm (with reducer). Oh wait, we now have the third great advantage of using the ESATTO microfocuser together with Celestron EdgeHD telescopes! In fact you can use it also to properly set the backfocus distance of your camera sensor! Take a look at this setup I have here: by adding the ESATTO after the focal reducer I still have plenty of space to let me use an OAG with an autoguider and a filter drawer or a motorized filter wheel. By adding this cooled camera I have my sensor at around 140mm from the telescope rear cell so, in order to have the perfect backfocus, this is what I do: I extend the drawtube for the missing length to reach the perfect backfocus position, in this case 6mm. I can also record the drawtube extension in the Virtual HandPad in order to easily recall it when needed. Then, with the telescope pointed at the night sky, I use the internal focuser to get sharp pictures, and I lock the primary mirror This way, during the night, I will be able to use the ESATTO only for micro focus adjustments that have no impact on telescope performance. By using the ESATTO microfocuser with EdgeHD telescopes you have a perfect focus management of your telescope that is very important, especially in astrophotography, in order to have the greatest performance. You can remotely control the focus and you avoid all the problems related to image shift and mirror flop. That’s why the ESATTO is the perfect microfocuser also for EdgeHD telescopes!
